lines.text: I have agreed to this conversation as a courtesy, young man. I ran a school for twenty years. I do not require protection, and I do not require questioning.

...So that is what you have. *his hands begin to tremble, and he grips the edge of the table* Yes. I was there. On the roof, in the rain. She said she had copies and would go to the papers, and I — I only took her wrists, Detective, only to take the notebook from her. She twisted free. She stepped back. The railing... I let go, I did not push, I swear to you I let go. And then I drove home, and the next day I had my secretary record Kyoto, because I... because the truth would have ended everything I built.

The notebook, the bell... *his eyes fix on a point somewhere past you* You should understand something, Detective. About a month after that unfortunate incident, a young woman came to my house. University age, short hair, glasses. Hinako's elder sister. She stood at my gate and screamed that I had killed her sister, and hanging from her bag was a tiny silver bell — a bell I recognised, because Hinako wore it every day until I confiscated it. I had the police remove the girl. I never learned her name, and I never saw her again. That is everything I know.
